A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GraphIDS and provide readable main text and Appendices A–D. Corresponding equations, all 14 tables, and all 12 figures could be matched. The rasterized appendix plots in v6 were inspected visually.

before.justification: v5 reports original intrusion-detection experiments, runtime and memory measurements, qualitative analyses, and component ablations in Section 4 and Appendices B–C.

after.justification: v6 retains the work's original benchmark results, computational measurements, qualitative analyses, and ablations in Section 4 and Appendices B–C.

M1.justification: The joint E-GraphSAGE/Transformer architecture, attention masking, reconstruction loss, and inference procedure are retained. v6 clarifies independent 512-flow attention windows, resolving v5's inconsistent description of a 32,768-embedding sequence. The window size and batch size already appear as 512 and 64 in v5's Table 14; this supports a documentation correction rather than an established method redesign.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate intrusion detection on NF-UNSW-NB15 and NF-CSE-CIC-IDS2018, each in v2 and v3 form. No dataset, attack population, or evaluated deployment scenario is added or removed. The fuller explanation of 20% sampling does not introduce new coverage.

E2.justification: Table 3 retains CBLOF, SAFE, Anomal-E, T-MAE, and SimpleAE. Appendix B retains the same CBLOF, HBOS, Isolation Forest, and PCA comparisons on Anomal-E embeddings and raw features. The revised discussion of baseline selection does not establish a new comparison method.

E3.justification: Section 4.5 replaces v5's stated linearly interpolated PR-AUC calculation with average precision computed by scikit-learn's average_precision_score without interpolation. This is a substantive correction to the reported evaluation metric, although unchanged numerical results do not establish that experiments were rerun. Split proportions, training budgets, and tabulated configurations remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C retains the same timestamp, positional-encoding, dropout, masking-ratio, and neighborhood-size ablations. Appendix B retains the precision-recall curves, attack-score distributions, embedding visualizations, and resource comparisons. Revised qualifications do not add or remove an analysis.

E5.justification: Tables 3 and 5 replace statements about statistical significance with highlighting based on best results and differences small relative to variation across seeds. Reporting of means, standard deviations, and unspecified multiple seeds is otherwise unchanged; no additional runs or statistical tests are established.

E6.justification: Numerical entries in all tables are unchanged, and the plots retain their outcomes. For example, Table 3 still reports GraphIDS PR-AUC of 0.9998 and macro F1 of 0.9961 on NF-UNSW-NB15-v3. No new result entries or measured performance improvements are reported; the metric-description correction belongs to E3.

T1.justification: The graph and flow definitions, reconstruction score and MSE loss in Equations 1–2, and positional-encoding formulation in Equation 3 are retained. Neither version provides theorems or proofs. The window notation and standard metric implementation are clarified without adding formal reasoning.

C1.justification: The architectural novelty claim remains, but the introduction and conclusion narrow the performance advantage to the strongest external baselines on the v3 datasets. Claims of demonstrated generalization to unseen attacks and practical real-time deployment are removed or qualified. Label-free learning is explicitly restricted to the reconstruction objective rather than the whole evaluation pipeline.

C2.justification: Section 4.6 replaces cross-version difficulty attribution with an explicit warning that feature and aggregation effects cannot be isolated, and interprets attention within individual windows. Section 4.3 identifies deployment time-window management as unevaluated. The conclusion changes the stability assumption from topology to behavior and presents single-host limitations more cautiously.

D1.justification: v6 explicitly documents separate graphs for each partition, no edges crossing partitions, and identical 20% NF-CSE-CIC-IDS2018 samples across methods. It clarifies window batching and discloses validation-only Anomal-E detector and hyperparameter selection in Appendix A. These refine existing experimental documentation; hardware, software versions, Table 14 hyperparameters, and code/model access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v6 removes Liu et al.'s dataset-error reference and revises the associated NetFlow provenance statement. It also qualifies Anomal-E's label independence and revises discussion of its target encoding and reported test-partition model selection. Other reference changes largely update capitalization or publication metadata for the same works.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites improve precision in the introduction, method description, evaluation, conclusion, and selected appendix paragraphs. Section order and Appendices A–D remain intact, with no substantial narrative restructuring. Bibliographic terminology and version-header text also receive limited edits.

P2.justification: Figures 4 and 9–12 change from vector graphics to raster images while preserving their plotted content. Tables 3 and 5 receive revised captions, Table 14 shortens two dataset headings, and text reflow shifts appendix pagination. No figure or table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: v6 improves reporting precision and aligns claims more closely with the evidence. It clarifies attention windows, partition isolation, shared sampling, and validation use; corrects the metric description and significance wording; and qualifies deployment and generalization claims. These changes make the retained experiments easier to interpret and reproduce, although the PDFs do not establish any change to the underlying experiments.
